slides.title: The Conformal Model As A Geometry Engine
slides.notes: Open by framing Chapter 13 as the moment when Part II stops treating Euclidean geometry as a collection of separate coordinate recipes. The lecture will lift points, encode planes and spheres as probes, and then use products and versors so distance, incidence, reflection, and rigid motion are all checked in one algebraic environment.

slides.title: A Null Basis Buys A Euclidean Metric
slides.notes: Spend time on the metric table before using any formula. The Euclidean basis vectors behave as usual, but the two added directions are null and coupled to each other. That single negative cross term is the mechanism that lets a quadratic Euclidean distance reappear as a bilinear conformal inner product.

slides.title: Embedding Points On The Null Cone
slides.notes: Use the cone drawing to make the lift feel geometric rather than syntactic. A finite point does not become just a coordinate vector with two extras attached; it lands on a null cone with a fixed weight. The quadratic infinity coefficient is precisely what stores enough information for later distance recovery.

slides.title: Distance Is An Inner Product After Normalization
slides.notes: Emphasize that the raw representative is projective in spirit, so weights matter. Once points are normalized, the conformal inner product gives squared Euclidean distance without returning to a special distance subroutine. This is the first operational payoff: metric facts become product-level facts.

slides.title: Vectors Become Geometric Probes
slides.notes: Present point, plane, and sphere probes as one family of zero tests. The object is not interrogated by a custom class method; it is represented by a vector and paired with a lifted point. The sign of the result then carries side, inside-outside, or distance information depending on the vector.

slides.title: Joins And Meets Share The Same Grammar
slides.notes: Use this as the algebraic grammar slide. Joins build an object from spanning points and the infinity vector, while meets extract intersections through duality and outer products. Students do not need every blade grade memorized today; they need to see that span and intersection have a common syntax.

slides.title: Distance And Angle Predicates Are Auditable
slides.notes: Turn the predicate grid into a programming checklist. Every geometric question should name its representative, its normalization, and the scalar expected from an inner product or contraction. This prevents code from mixing unweighted representatives with Euclidean objects and makes angle or contact tests reproducible.

slides.title: Euclidean Operators Preserve Infinity
slides.notes: Make the preservation of the infinity vector the gatekeeper for Euclidean behavior. A conformal map may preserve angles while moving infinity, but then it is no longer an ordinary Euclidean motion. Rotations, translations, and reflections keep infinity fixed, so the distance identity remains valid after transformation.

slides.title: Flats Separate Position From Direction
slides.notes: Connect this slide back to the homogeneous and Plucker chapters. A line or plane has finite placement data and ideal direction data. Translations change the moment or offset, but not the ideal direction. That separation is why the infinity vector is not an ornament; it is part of the flat's Euclidean meaning.

slides.title: Plane Reflection As A Uniform Operation
slides.notes: Use reflection to show why the conformal model is operationally attractive. The dual plane vector is both a predicate and a reflecting element. Signed distances flip, applying the reflection twice returns the original object, and the same sandwich idea can act on richer objects than isolated points.

slides.title: Motors Package Rigid Motion And Interpolation
slides.notes: Treat the screw path as the proper-motion counterpart to reflection. Motors compose rotations and translations inside the conformal algebra, and logarithm-based interpolation follows a generator rather than blending matrices entry by entry. The crucial teaching point is that every intermediate pose should remain a valid rigid motion.

slides.title: Differentiating A Moving Mirror
slides.notes: Use the moving mirror to reconnect Chapter 13 with geometric differentiation. When the plane rotates about an offset hinge, both the normal and the offset change. A finite-difference check is not a formality here; it protects against forgetting the offset derivative and misreading the velocity field.

slides.title: Operational Euclidean Geometry
slides.notes: Close by naming the practical contract. A conformal implementation should check nullness, weight, metric preservation, infinity preservation, incidence residuals, and motion endpoints. The chapter's theme is not more coordinates for their own sake; it is a representation where Euclidean questions become algebraic operations with inspectable residuals.
